newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firm, demand steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firm, demand steady.

text.p: Steady heating oil demand on Monday helped NWE gas oil cargo premiums shrug off milder European weather and defend Friday's gains, but barge premiums were under pressure from canal ice blockages, trader said.

"There has been healthy buying of Russian. We are clearing some length," a cargo trader said. Benchmark Feb IPE tumbled $7.25 to $219 a tonne as NYMEX crude and products threw off earlier gains. Milder European weather also helped the fall.
Russian heating oil traded unchanged at Feb +$7.50 cif NWE and French grade was done at Feb +$9 cif Hamburg. Low sulphur cargoes were offered at Feb +$16 into Brest and bid at +$14.
On barges, ice blockages that have slowed volumes eased slightly late on Monday but traders still estimated it would take 10 days to thaw fully throughout ARA and inland.

Trade was quieter, with buyers holding out for lower prices. Refinery grade heating oil traded unchanged to slightly easier at Feb IPE +$6.50 fob Amsterdam and Feb +$9 fob Rotterdam. Low sulphur diesel was Feb +$10.50/13.
Traders said that of the 261,700 tonnes of gas oil to be delivered on the IPE January contract, about 140,000 tonnes would be delivered to Antwerp and 121,700 to Amsterdam.
